en afløser.explanation: "En afløser" means "a substitute". Do not mix it up with "en afløsning" (a relief). "En afløser" is the person: "Afløseren kommer klokken otte" (The substitute comes at eight o'clock). "En afløsning" is the act of taking over: "Natholdet får afløsning klokken seks" (The night team gets relief at six o'clock).

en afløsning.explanation: "En afløsning" means "a relief / replacement". When a caregiver at home gets help so they can take a break, Danish uses this word too: "Hun får afløsning to timer om ugen" (She gets relief two hours a week). Do not mix it up with "en afløser" (a substitute). "En afløsning" is the act of taking over, and "en afløser" is the person: "Afløseren kommer klokken otte" (The substitute comes at eight o'clock).

en afrejse.explanation: "En afrejse" means "a departure". It is built from "af" (off) and the verb "at rejse" (to travel). Do not mix it up with "en afgang" (a departure). "En afgang" is when a train or bus leaves a stop: "Afgang fra spor 3 er klokken ti" (Departure from platform 3 is at ten o'clock).

en afrikaner.explanation: "En afrikaner" means "an African". It is built from "Afrika" (Africa). Danish writes it with a small first letter: "afrikaner", not "Afrikaner".

en afsked.explanation: "En afsked" means "a farewell". To say you say goodbye to someone, use "at tage" (to take) and "med" (with): "Jeg tager afsked med min ven" (I say goodbye to my friend).

en afslutning.explanation: "En afslutning" means "an ending". It comes from the verb "at afslutte" (to finish). In a Danish school, "afslutning" is also the party at the end of the school year: "Vi har afslutning i skolen i morgen" (We have the end-of-year party at school tomorrow).

en afstand.explanation: "En afstand" means "a distance". To ask how far away a place is, say "afstanden til" (the distance to): "Hvad er afstanden til stationen?" (What is the distance to the station?) To tell someone to stay back, say "Hold afstand!" (Keep your distance!)

en afstemning.explanation: "En afstemning" means "a vote". Do not mix it up with "et valg" (an election). "En afstemning" is a vote on a question: "Der er afstemning om forslaget" (There is a vote on the proposal). "Et valg" is when people choose a person: "Klubben har valg til bestyrelsen" (The club has an election for the board).

en aftale.explanation: "En aftale" means "an appointment / agreement". When you book a time with someone and want to move it, say "Kan vi flytte aftalen til fredag?" (Can we move the appointment to Friday?) When two people agree on something, you can say "Det er en aftale!" (It's a deal!)

en aften.explanation: "En aften" means "an evening". To say "tonight", use "i aften": "Vi ses i aften" (See you tonight).

en aftenrutine.explanation: "En aftenrutine" means "an evening routine". It is built from "aften" (evening) and "rutine" (routine). The part "aften" is also in "aftensmad" (dinner): "Hvad skal vi have til aftensmad?" (What are we having for dinner?)

en aftenskole.explanation: "En aftenskole" means "an evening class". In Denmark, adults can take courses in the evening at a school of this kind, in subjects such as languages, cooking or painting. It is built from "aften" (evening) and "skole" (school).

en aftentur.explanation: "En aftentur" means "an evening walk". It is built from "aften" (evening) and "tur" (walk, trip). To suggest a walk without saying when, use "tur" with "at tage" (to take): "Skal vi tage en tur?" (Shall we go for a walk?)

en aftrækker.explanation: "En aftrækker" means "a trigger", as in the part of a gun. Do not use it for something that sets off a reaction. That is "en udløser" (a trigger): "Stress kan være en udløser for migræne" (Stress can be a trigger for migraine).

en afveksling.explanation: "En afveksling" means "a variety / change". To say someone does something for a change, use "til afveksling": "Til afveksling lavede han mad" (For a change, he cooked).

en afvigelse.explanation: "En afvigelse" means "a deviation". It comes from the verb "at afvige" (to deviate).

en agent.explanation: "En agent" means "an agent", as in a person who handles deals for an actor or athlete. When you talk about a spy, it has a different meaning: "en hemmelig agent" (a secret agent).

en agurk.explanation: "En agurk" means "a cucumber". To talk about cucumbers kept in a jar, use "syltede agurker" (pickled cucumbers): "Der er syltede agurker i glasset" (There are pickled cucumbers in the jar).

en airbag.explanation: "En airbag" means "an airbag". When you write "the airbag", double the g: "airbaggen", not "airbagen".

en airfryer.explanation: "En airfryer" means "an air fryer". Danish writes it as one word, "airfryer", not as two words like English.

en aktie.explanation: "En aktie" means "a share", as in a part of a company. To say which company, add "i" (in): "Hun ejer aktier i et dansk firma" (She owns shares in a Danish company).

en aktiekurs.explanation: "En aktiekurs" means "a share price". It is built from "aktie" (share) and "kurs" (rate). To say the price goes down, use "at falde" (to fall): "Aktiekursen faldt i dag" (The share price fell today).

en aktivitet.explanation: "En aktivitet" means "an activity". When a school or club plans things for a group to do, Danish uses the plural: "Der er mange aktiviteter for børn i sommerferien" (There are many activities for children in the summer holiday).

en akvariefisk.explanation: "En akvariefisk" means "an aquarium fish". It is built from "akvarium" (aquarium) and "fisk" (fish). For more than one fish, the word stays the same, with no ending: "Vi har fem akvariefisk" (We have five aquarium fish).

en alarm.explanation: "En alarm" means "an alarm". When a warning sounds, say "Alarmen går!" (The alarm is going off!) To set a wake-up alarm on your phone, say "Jeg stiller en alarm til klokken syv" (I set an alarm for seven o'clock).

en alarmklokke.explanation: "En alarmklokke" means "an alarm bell". It is built from "alarm" (alarm) and "klokke" (bell). The part "klokke" also means "clock" when you ask the time: "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

en albue.explanation: "En albue" means "an elbow". Danish can use "albuen" (the elbow) for your own elbow: "Jeg har slået albuen" (I hit my elbow), literally "I hit the elbow".

en alder.explanation: "En alder" means "an age". To ask how old someone is, Danish does not use "alder". It uses "gammel" (old): "Hvor gammel er du?" (How old are you?) To say "at my age", use "i min alder": "Det er svært i min alder" (It is hard at my age).

en algoritme.explanation: "En algoritme" means "an algorithm". Danish spells it without an "h": "algoritme", not "algorithm".

en alkoholiker.explanation: "En alkoholiker" means "an alcoholic". It is built from "alkohol" (alcohol). Danish spells it with "k", not "c".

en allergi.explanation: "En allergi" means "an allergy". To name what you react to, put its name in front of "allergi" as one word: "en pollenallergi" (a pollen allergy).

en alliance.explanation: "En alliance" means "an alliance". To say who the alliance is with, add "med" (with): "Vi har en alliance med vores naboer" (We have an alliance with our neighbors).

en allieret.explanation: "En allieret" means "an ally". When you talk about history, "de allierede" (the allies) are the countries that fought Germany in World War II: "Danmark blev befriet af de allierede i 1945" (Denmark was freed by the Allies in 1945).

en altan.explanation: "En altan" means "a balcony". The part "altan" is also in "en altankasse" (a balcony planter box): "Jeg har blomster i en altankasse" (I have flowers in a balcony planter box).

en amatør.explanation: "En amatør" means "an amateur". To call a person who does a poor job an amateur, say "Sikke en amatør!" (What an amateur!) This is an insult.

en ambassade.explanation: "En ambassade" means "an embassy". To say you are going to the embassy, use "på" (at): "Vi skal på ambassaden i morgen" (We are going to the embassy tomorrow).

en ambassadør.explanation: "En ambassadør" means "an ambassador". When a well-known person speaks for a cause, the word fits too: "Hun er ambassadør for en velgørenhedsorganisation" (She is an ambassador for a charity).

en ambition.explanation: "En ambition" means "an ambition". To say someone has big goals, use "at have" (to have) and the plural: "De har store ambitioner for firmaet" (They have big ambitions for the firm).

en ambulance.explanation: "En ambulance" means "an ambulance". In Denmark, you call the emergency number 112 to get one: "Ring til 112!" (Call 112!)

en amerikaner.explanation: "En amerikaner" means "an American". It is built from "Amerika" (America). Danish writes it with a small first letter: "amerikaner", not "Amerikaner". In a Danish bakery, "en amerikaner" is also a flat, round cake with icing: "Vi køber to amerikanere hos bageren" (We buy two amerikaner cakes at the baker).

en analyse.explanation: "En analyse" means "an analysis". To say what you analyze, add "af" (of): "Vi laver en analyse af tallene" (We do an analysis of the numbers).

en ananas.explanation: "En ananas" means "a pineapple". Danish doubles the s before an ending, so "the pineapple" is "ananassen" with two s's.

en anbefaling.explanation: "En anbefaling" means "a recommendation". To say who told you about a place, use "på anbefaling af" (on the recommendation of): "Vi kom på anbefaling af en ven" (We came on a friend's recommendation).

en and.explanation: "En and" means "a duck". The form for "the duck" is "anden". The same spelling is also the word for "the other". To talk about the duck, say "Anden svømmer" (The duck swims). To point to the other one of two things, say "Jeg tager den anden" (I take the other one).

en andel.explanation: "En andel" means "a share / portion". To talk about a part of a whole group, use "andelen af" (the share of): "Andelen af ældre vokser" (The share of older people is growing). The word "andel" is also in "en andelsbolig" (a cooperative apartment): "Vi bor i en andelsbolig" (We live in a cooperative apartment).

en andelsbolig.explanation: "En andelsbolig" means "a cooperative apartment". It is built from "andel" (share) and "bolig" (home). In Denmark, the monthly fee you pay for one is called "boligafgift" (housing fee).

en anekdote.explanation: "En anekdote" means "an anecdote". Danish spells it with "k", not "c": "anekdote".

en anelse.explanation: "En anelse" means "a hint / slight idea". To say something is a touch better, put "en anelse" before the describing word: "Det er en anelse bedre" (It is a touch better). To ask whether someone has any idea, say "Har du en anelse om hvorfor?" (Do you have any idea why?)

en anfører.explanation: "En anfører" means "a captain (team)". It comes from the verb "at anføre" (to lead).

en angriber.explanation: "En angriber" means "a forward / attacker". Outside sport, when someone attacks a person, use it for "attacker": "Angriberen løb væk" (The attacker ran away).

en anholdelse.explanation: "En anholdelse" means "an arrest". To say a person was arrested, use "anholdt" (arrested) with "blive" (to be): "Han blev anholdt i går" (He was arrested yesterday).

en ankel.explanation: "En ankel" means "an ankle". To say you sprained your ankle, use "at forstuve" (to sprain): "Jeg har forstuvet anklen" (I have sprained my ankle).

en anklage.explanation: "En anklage" means "an accusation". It comes from the verb "at anklage" (to accuse). To say someone brings an accusation, use "at rejse" (to raise): "De rejser en anklage mod ham" (They bring an accusation against him).

en anklager.explanation: "En anklager" means "a prosecutor". Do not mix it up with "en anklage" (an accusation). "En anklager" is a person: "Anklageren taler i retten" (The prosecutor speaks in court). "En anklage" is a statement against someone: "Anklagen er alvorlig" (The accusation is serious).

en ankomst.explanation: "En ankomst" means "an arrival". To say "on arrival", use "ved ankomsten": "Ved ankomsten skal du vise dit pas" (On arrival you must show your passport).

en ankomsthal.explanation: "En ankomsthal" means "an arrivals hall". It is built from "ankomst" (arrival) and "hal" (hall). The part "hal" is also in "en idrætshal" (a sports hall): "Vi spiller håndbold i idrætshallen" (We play handball in the sports hall).

en anledning.explanation: "En anledning" means "an occasion". When you talk about a reason to do something, the word means "reason": "Jeg har ingen anledning til at klage" (I have no reason to complain).

en anmeldelse.explanation: "En anmeldelse" means "a review", as in a written opinion of a book, film or restaurant. When you report a crime to the police, the word is "en politianmeldelse": "Jeg vil gerne lave en politianmeldelse" (I would like to file a police report).

en anmelder.explanation: "En anmelder" means "a reviewer / critic". When someone reports a crime to the police, that person is "anmelderen": "Anmelderen ringede til politiet" (The person who reported the crime called the police).

en anmodning.explanation: "En anmodning" means "a request". It is a formal word. For an everyday request, use "at bede om" (to ask for): "Jeg vil bede om hjælp" (I would like to ask for help).

en annonce.explanation: "En annonce" means "an advertisement". For an ad on TV, use "en reklame" (a commercial): "Der er en reklame i fjernsynet" (There is a commercial on TV).

en ansat.explanation: "En ansat" means "an employee". To say you work for a company, use "er ansat" (am employed): "Jeg er ansat her" (I am employed here).

en ansigtscreme.explanation: "En ansigtscreme" means "a face cream". Danish spells "cream" as "creme", and joins "ansigt" (face) to it with an "s".

en ansættelse.explanation: "En ansættelse" means "an employment / hiring". To say who is being hired, add "af" (of): "ansættelsen af en ny chef" (the hiring of a new boss).

en ansættelseskontrakt.explanation: "En ansættelseskontrakt" means "an employment contract". It is built from "ansættelse" (employment) and "kontrakt" (contract). To say you signed it, use "at skrive under på" (to sign): "Jeg skrev under på ansættelseskontrakten i går" (I signed the employment contract yesterday).

en ansættelsessamtale.explanation: "En ansættelsessamtale" means "a job interview". It is built from "ansættelse" (employment) and "samtale" (conversation). Another word for the same thing is "en jobsamtale": "Jeg har en jobsamtale i morgen" (I have a job interview tomorrow).

en ansøgning.explanation: "En ansøgning" means "an application". To say what you apply for, add "om" (for): "Hun skriver en ansøgning om et job" (She writes an application for a job).

en ansøgningsfrist.explanation: "En ansøgningsfrist" means "an application deadline". It is built from "ansøgning" (application) and "frist" (deadline). To say you meet it, use "at overholde" (to keep to): "Du skal overholde ansøgningsfristen" (You must meet the application deadline).

en antagelse.explanation: "En antagelse" means "an assumption". It comes from the verb "at antage" (to assume). To say an assumption is fair, use "rimelig" (reasonable): "Det er en rimelig antagelse" (That is a fair assumption).

en antydning.explanation: "En antydning" means "a hint". To say someone hinted at something, use "give en antydning af" (give a hint of): "Hun gav en antydning af, at hun ville flytte" (She dropped a hint that she would move). Do not mix it up with "en anelse" (a slight idea). "En anelse" is what you have yourself: "Jeg har en anelse om svaret" (I have a slight idea of the answer).

en apoteker.explanation: "En apoteker" means "a pharmacist". It is built from "apotek" (pharmacy). To say you are going to the pharmacy, use "på apoteket": "Jeg skal på apoteket" (I am going to the pharmacy).

en app.explanation: "En app" means "an app". To tell someone to open one, use "at åbne" (to open): "Åbn appen" (Open the app).

en appelsin.explanation: "En appelsin" means "an orange", as in the fruit. For the color, Danish uses "orange": "en orange bold" (an orange ball).

en araber.explanation: "En araber" means "an Arab". Danish writes it with a small first letter: "araber", not "Araber". To name the language, use "arabisk" (Arabic): "Han taler arabisk" (He speaks Arabic).

en arbejdsbyrde.explanation: "En arbejdsbyrde" means "a workload". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "byrde" (burden). To say the work is too much, call the workload heavy: "en tung arbejdsbyrde" (a heavy workload).

en arbejdsdag.explanation: "En arbejdsdag" means "a working day". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "dag" (day). To say a day at work is long, say "en lang arbejdsdag" (a long working day).

en arbejdsgiver.explanation: "En arbejdsgiver" means "an employer". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "at give" (to give). The ending "giver" is also in "en rådgiver" (an adviser), someone who gives råd (advice): "Hun er min rådgiver" (She is my adviser).

en arbejdsopgave.explanation: "En arbejdsopgave" means "a work task". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "opgave" (task). To say you have been given a new one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg har fået en ny arbejdsopgave" (I have a new work task).

en arbejdsplads.explanation: "En arbejdsplads" means "a workplace". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "plads" (place). The part "plads" also means room or space: "Der er plads til alle" (There is room for everyone).

en arbejdsskade.explanation: "En arbejdsskade" means "a work injury". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "skade" (injury). In Denmark, a work injury can give you the right to compensation.

en arbejdstager.explanation: "En arbejdstager" means "an employee". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "at tage" (to take): the one who takes work. The opposite is "en arbejdsgiver" (an employer): "Arbejdsgiveren betaler arbejdstageren" (The employer pays the employee).

en arbejdstilladelse.explanation: "En arbejdstilladelse" means "a work permit". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "tilladelse" (permission). To say you are applying for one, use "at søge om" (to apply for): "Jeg søger om en arbejdstilladelse" (I am applying for a work permit).

en arkitekt.explanation: "En arkitekt" means "an architect". Danish spells it with "k", not "ch": "arkitekt".

en arm.explanation: "En arm" means "an arm". Danish can use "armen" (the arm) for your own arm: "Hun har brækket armen" (She has broken her arm), literally "She has broken the arm".

en armbøjning.explanation: "En armbøjning" means "a push-up". It is built from "arm" (arm) and "bøjning" (bending).

en arrangør.explanation: "En arrangør" means "an organizer". It comes from the verb "at arrangere" (to organize). To say what someone organizes, add "af" (of): "Han er arrangør af koncerten" (He is the organizer of the concert).

en art.explanation: "En art" means "a species". To talk about an animal that may die out, use "truet" (endangered): "Bjørnen er en truet art" (The bear is an endangered species).

en artikel.explanation: "En artikel" means "an article", as in a piece of writing. In grammar, the word also names "en" and "et": "På dansk er en og et artikler" (In Danish, en and et are articles).

en arv.explanation: "En arv" means "an inheritance". When you talk about something passed down, such as traditions, use "en kulturarv" (a cultural heritage): "Eventyr er en del af vores kulturarv" (Fairy tales are part of our cultural heritage).

en arving.explanation: "En arving" means "an heir". It belongs to the same family as "arv" (inheritance). To talk about a royal heir, say "arving til tronen" (heir to the throne): "Prinsen er arving til tronen" (The prince is heir to the throne).

en asiat.explanation: "En asiat" means "an Asian". Danish writes it with a small first letter: "asiat", not "Asiat". To name the person's country, use the nationality word for that country: "en thailænder" (a Thai person).

en assistent.explanation: "En assistent" means "an assistant". Danish ends it with "-ent", not "-ant": "assistent".

en astronaut.explanation: "En astronaut" means "an astronaut". To say what you dream of being, use "at blive" (to become): "Jeg vil gerne blive astronaut" (I would like to become an astronaut).

en asylansøger.explanation: "En asylansøger" means "an asylum seeker". It is built from "asyl" (asylum) and "ansøger" (applicant). To say someone asks for asylum, use "at søge asyl" (to seek asylum): "Hun søger asyl i Danmark" (She is seeking asylum in Denmark).

en atmosfære.explanation: "En atmosfære" means "an atmosphere", as in the layer of gases around the Earth. When you talk about the feeling in a place, the word fits too: "Der er en god atmosfære på kontoret" (There is a good atmosphere in the office).

en attitude.explanation: "En attitude" means "an attitude". In Danish, it means a bold, confident way of acting: "Han har attitude" (He has attitude). For a view or opinion, use "en holdning" (a stance): "Hun har en positiv holdning" (She has a positive attitude).

en aubergine.explanation: "En aubergine" means "an eggplant". Danish uses the French spelling "aubergine", the same as British English.

en auktion.explanation: "En auktion" means "an auction". The word is also in "et auktionshus" (an auction house): "Vi sælger billedet hos auktionshuset" (We sell the painting at the auction house).

en autograf.explanation: "En autograf" means "an autograph". Danish spells it with "f", not "ph": "autograf". To ask a famous person for one, say "Må jeg få en autograf?" (May I have an autograph?)

en autoritet.explanation: "En autoritet" means "an authority". To say someone is trusted because of what they know, use "på området" (in the field): "Hun er en autoritet på området" (She is an authority in the field). For government offices, use "myndighederne" (the authorities): "Myndighederne undersøger sagen" (The authorities are looking into the case).
